source_text: Homilia in illud: Ego vado ad patrem meum Κυρίλλου ἐπισκόπου Ἱεροσολύμων εἰς τὸ "Ἐγὼ πορεύομαι πρὸς τὸν πατέρα μου· καὶ ὃ ἐὰν αἰτήσητε ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου, τοῦτο ποιήσω, ἵνα δοξασθῇ ὁ πατὴρ ἐν τῷ υἱῷ".
thought_title: Title and Gospel text of the homily
orientation: This is the opening title of Cyril of Jerusalem's homily, giving the Gospel saying on which he will preach.
pass_a_gloss: Homily on that text: I am going to my Father. Of Cyril, bishop of Jerusalem, on the text: "I am going to my Father; and whatever you ask in my name, this I will do, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son."

lemmas.gloss: so that he may be glorified

choices.why: The genre term for a preached discourse; 'homily' is the standard English equivalent and matches the work's title.
The preposition with the articular quotation indicates the subject of the homily; 'on the text' makes the function clear.
The present tense of the Gospel saying is preserved; 'I am going' keeps the ongoing sense.
The indefinite relative with subjunctive is rendered as 'whatever you ask' to keep the open condition.

choices.english: so that he may be glorified
choices.why: The purpose clause with aorist subjunctive passive is rendered with 'so that' and the passive 'may be glorified' to preserve the divine passive.
rejected: that the Father may be glorified
in order that he be glorified

bible_refs.note: The quoted Greek text matches the Gospel saying: Ἐγὼ πορεύομαι πρὸς τὸν πατέρα μου· καὶ ὃ ἐὰν αἰτήσητε ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου, τοῦτο ποιήσω, ἵνα δοξασθῇ ὁ πατὴρ ἐν τῷ υἱῷ.

pass_b_english: In the statements made about both his divinity and his humanity, he places the “I,” so that the meaning of the words is shown by their sequence, while the discernment of the natures is shown by the difference in what is said. And because he speaks in both cases as though about one person, he signifies the union of the person.

last_rejected.why: "As though" adds a false note of appearance; ὡς here means "as" in the sense of identity, not pretense.
last_rejected.ruling: ὡς περὶ ἑνὸς προσώπου naturally rendered 'as though about one person'; ὡς with περί commonly conveys comparison, not strict identity.

problems.why: Same Greek term (διάκρισις) rendered two ways; reader may think different concepts.

problems.quote: the distinction of the natures is shown
problems.why: Same concept rendered with different words across parallel sections.
problems.fix: Use one consistent English word (e.g., 'distinction') throughout.

problems.fix: Clarify whether this is Cyril's own voice or a cited text.

fixed: The speaker problem is not real: the English is Cyril's own voice, as in the source, and no quotation is indicated.
